title: JointDiff: Bridging Continuous and Discrete in Multi-Agent Trajectory Generation
claim: A single model jointly generates continuous trajectories and synchronized discrete events through iterative denoising, steered by weak or textual guidance.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; input/guidance box feeds denoising chain with 3D bars
description: The figure has two parts. On the left, a yellow box labeled 'Continuous trajectories / Discrete events' shows colored player dots and a row of colored circles along a time axis T. An arrow leads to a gray 'JointDiff' box, then to a refined yellow box at step s−1. Below, a grey 'Observations' box and a blue 'Guidance' speech-bubble box give two inputs, a weak-possessor list and a natural-language text prompt, and both point into JointDiff. On the right, a denoising chain runs from s=S to s=0. Each step shows scattered colored dots that become coherent trajectories. Under each are 3D bar charts of possession events per agent over time T. Curved arrows labeled p_θ and q mark the reverse and forward processes. The eye goes first to the colorful trajectories and the bars.
caption: JointDiff. Our model jointly generates continuous trajectories and discrete events, with guidance provided through either weak-possessor information or natural language text. Stars (⋆) refer to the initial timestep.
abstract: Generative models often treat continuous data and discrete events as separate processes, creating a gap in modeling complex systems where they interact synchronously. To bridge this gap, we introduce JointDiff, a novel diffusion framework designed to unify these two processes by simultaneously generating continuous spatio-temporal data and synchronous discrete events. We demonstrate its efficacy in the sports domain by simultaneously modeling multi-agent trajectories and key possession events. This joint modeling is validated with non-controllable generation and two novel controllable generation scenarios: weak-possessor-guidance, which offers flexible semantic control over game dynamics through a simple list of intended ball possessors, and text-guidance, which enables fine-grained, language-driven generation. To enable the conditioning with these guidance signals, we introduce CrossGuid, an effective conditioning operation for multi-agent domains. We also share a new unified sports benchmark enhanced with textual descriptions for soccer and football datasets. JointDiff achieves state-of-the-art performance, demonstrating that joint modeling is crucial for building realistic and controllable generative models for interactive systems. https://guillem-cf.github.io/JointDiff/
